The remote's own token must also allow the profile action there; the remote shows no file path. Compact and reset are never sent to a remote.

remotes.description: Go backend only. Names of remote entries (files in the remotes folder, see remote.schema.json) the tool may use as remote:<name>/... . Needed with allow_remote, and only then. Each name must have a valid file, checked when the session loads.

load_tool.description: Go backend only. The runner for the profile's tools.lazy tools (MCP and extension tools only; a native tool is always listed and never lazy): with no arguments it lists them (name and one-line summary), with names it describes them (name, id, description, inputSchema), with run and arguments it runs one by its exact name or mcp:<server>:<tool>. A lazy tool is never in the model's tools array, so using load_tool never changes the array a provider caches. Read-only, and it takes no keys. A profile with tools.lazy needs this key: without it the profile is refused at load. Off unless this key is present. Needs load_tool in tool_definition_paths. A sub-agent has it too, over the owning profile's lazy set, unless its own tools key leaves it out; it describes and runs only the tools its own catalog holds.

task.description: Persistent session task-plan policy. The task tool is exposed only when configured and its definition manifest is supplied.

statecontext.description: Task statuses and limit included in statecontext snapshots.

mode.description: items lists the matching records. summary adds a count per status and lists in full only the tasks named in detail_statuses, so a large section stays small; the model fetches the rest with the tool. Counts and the listed records come from one read.

detail_statuses.description: Only with mode summary: statuses listed in full, each of which must be in statuses.

max_batch_ops.description: Most operations one task call may pass in ops.

storage_dir.description: Persistent task-plan directory. The harness stores tasks.json inside it. A configured relative path resolves from the session cwd (setting.cwd). When omitted, the default lives under the selected profile's tool_storage root (under the cwd when no profile is selected). An absolute path is used as-is. A store is shared by every profile and session that resolves to the same path: an absolute path, or the same configured relative value (which lands in one path under the cwd).

code_context.description: Go backend only. Per task, a list of exact source ranges, read(path, start, end), each with a description and the hashes of what was read. read prints a range and saves it (with a description, saves it without printing); get prints each range's current code; find searches the task's saved descriptions and paths. A range whose saved bytes now occur exactly once elsewhere in the file is moved there (relocate); otherwise a range whose lines no longer hold the saved bytes is listed as stale for the caller to re-read and update, never printed as code. The tool never computes a new range from edits. The path rules are its own (read_style): without paths it reaches the workspace only. Needs code_context in tool_definition_paths.

storage_dir.description: Directory of the task files (<task>.json). A configured relative path resolves from the session cwd (setting.cwd). When omitted, the default lives under the selected profile's tool_storage root (under the cwd when no profile is selected). An absolute path is used as-is. Entries are shared by every profile and session that resolves to the same path: an absolute path, or the same configured relative value (which lands in one path under the cwd).

max_entries.description: Most entries one task may hold.

max_description_chars.description: Longest description of one entry, or of a task (task_description), in characters.

max_range_lines.description: Most lines one entry may read.

max_file_bytes.description: Largest file a range is read from; a larger one is refused on read and update and shows as stale on get.

max_output_bytes.description: Most bytes of code blocks one get prints (about 100K tokens by default; a ceiling, not a target). Blocks of the highest priority numbers are left out first and listed by id; get them with ids, which takes ranges such as "1-20".

max_storage_bytes.description: Largest task file; a write that would exceed it is refused.

relocate.description: Move a range whose saved bytes are no longer at its lines but occur exactly once elsewhere in the file (as many lines, the same length and SHA-256) to where they are now, and save the move. Off: such a range is stale.

default_priority.description: Priority of a range saved by read without one.

max_find_results.description: Most entries one find shows; the rest are counted.

max_scan_tasks.description: Most tasks a call without a task lists, most recently written first.

max_batch_items.description: Most items one read or update call may hold; they are saved in one write.

statecontext.description: Selected records included in statecontext snapshots. Types are dynamic; specify each included type, optional exact-match filter, and limit.

group_by.description: Dot-separated field path. Replaces the records with a count per value at that path; each group carries the filter of a records list call that fetches it. The scan is bounded by max_scan_records and max_scan_bytes, and at_least reports a truncated scan. Cannot be combined with limit, and the path cannot also be a filter key.

storage_dir.description: Records root directory. A configured relative path resolves from the session cwd (setting.cwd). When omitted, the default lives under the selected profile's tool_storage root (under the cwd when no profile is selected). An absolute path is used as-is. A store is shared by every profile and session that resolves to the same path: an absolute path, or the same configured relative value (which lands in one path under the cwd).

max_query_bytes.description: Largest search query, in bytes, the records tool's search operation accepts.

request_draft.description: User response timeout and draft-size policy for request_draft.

skill.description: Loads skill instructions by name from the global root's libraries.skill_dirs. Read-only.

max_bytes.description: Instruction bytes returned per call. A longer skill is cut and the result says so.

subagent.description: Go backend only. Lets the model hand a task to a separate agent that runs with a fresh context and returns only its final answer. May start with no agent, which is the case for a new project whose model creates its own; it then needs agents or agents_dir to be present, even if empty, and the tool definition sample/tools/native/subagent.json. A child's tools are resolved like a profile's (its run settings are its caller's, with its own model, instructions and run limits): it has every tool the session registers (native, extension and MCP, load_tool and the subagent tool included), minus the profile's tools.deny and the deny of every local run above it, narrowed only by its agent's own tools key; nesting is bounded by max_depth and the run caps.

agents_dir_missing_ok.description: When true, an agents_dir entry that does not exist is skipped instead of being a configuration error, so one toolset can list a general folder and each project's own folder (for example .jad/subagents), which a new project may not have. A path that exists but is not a directory is still an error, and the session then has no agent from it. Default false.

agents_dir_override.description: When true, an agent folder in a later agents_dir entry replaces an agent of the same name from an earlier entry (the replaced agent keeps its place), so a project folder can adapt a general agent. An inline agent is never replaced, and without this a name defined twice is an error. Default false.

agents_dir.description: Directories holding one folder per agent. A relative path resolves from the session's cwd; ~ is expanded; a directory that does not exist is a configuration error. The folder name is the agent name (1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens; folders starting with a dot are skipped). A folder holds agent.json (same keys as an inline agent, see agent.schema.json; relative paths inside it resolve from the folder) and/or prompt.md (the prompt text, placed after instructions and before prompt_documents). A folder with neither is an error. Agents defined here and in agents are all available; the same name twice is an error. Folders are read again each time a message starts a run, so an agent created during a run is usable from the next message.

agents.description: Agents by name (1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens), defined inline. May be empty or absent when agents_dir supplies the agents.

description.description: Shown to the model in the tool description, so keep it short.

model.description: Model for this agent. In a catalog-layout session a value that does not end in .json is a model ID '<category>/<name>' of the models catalog; the agent may name any model of it, not only those its caller's profile lists. A value ending in .json is a model file, relative to the agent's folder and must stay inside it (no .., absolute path or symlink leaving the folder). A legacy session reads every value as a file path (relative to the session directory for an inline agent). Absent means the calling session's model.

instructions.description: System prompt of the agent. The calling session's prompt is not used.

prompt_documents.description: Files appended to the agent's prompt after instructions (and after prompt.md for a folder agent), each separated by a blank line. A relative path is taken from the session's cwd, or from the agent's folder for a folder agent; ~ is expanded. The files are read when the session loads, and a missing file is a configuration error. The calling session's own prompt_documents are not used.

tools.description: The agent's own narrowing of its tools, written like a profile's tools block. Its tools are resolved like a profile's: with no tools key it has every tool the session registers (every native and extension tool, every MCP tool, and the subagent tool while max_depth allows nesting), minus the session profile's tools.deny and, for one call, the tools.deny of every run above it (a calling agent's, a profile_message caller's). An array is the allow list: native tools by name, mcp:<server>:<tool> (the server id from mcp_servers and the tool name the server reports) and mcp:<server>:* (every loaded tool of that server); an object has allow and deny arrays of the same entries, and deny wins. A name that names no enabled tool is a configuration error that lists the enabled ones. A list that names only async, exec, tool_smith, subagent, profile_message and load_tool (the old opt-in names) restricts nothing: it is ignored with a warning, so remove it. An agent that has exec (or tool_smith, profile_message, or subagent when max_depth is 2 or more) can change files: it takes the checkpoint like a write and runs to its end instead of being handed off unless tools.native.subagent.background_writers is on; an agent whose tools leave none of them is a reader.

toolset.description: One toolset file or a list of them, each '<category>/<name>' under the tools catalog (catalog-layout session only). The agent takes its tools, with their settings, and its MCP servers from it (or them) instead of the session's own toolset, so the profile does not have to register them and the parent never sees them. 'tools' still narrows within it and its mcp:<server>:<tool> entries are resolved against this file's servers only. The profile's tools.deny and each tool's own paths still apply. The toolset's own subagent entry is ignored; an agent that names a toolset may still list subagent, which is the session's tool. A sub-agent's toolset must not set tools.native.profile_message. An unknown toolset is a configuration error that lists the available ones. Given a list, the toolsets merge in order: when two name the same native tool or MCP server the first listed wins, with a warning, and only the first toolset with hooks supplies hooks (a later one's hooks are ignored with a warning). Absent means the session's toolset.

max_tool_rounds.description: Most tool rounds of one run.

max_run_tokens.description: Most tokens one run may use before it starts another provider round. Absent means no cap.

auto_compaction.description: Whether this agent's child compacts its own transcript when it grows. Absent follows the session's compaction.auto_enabled, or is on when compaction_trigger_tokens is set.

compaction_trigger_tokens.description: Input size, in tokens, at which this agent's child compacts. Absent uses the session's compaction.trigger_tokens, which is sized for the master's model, so set it for a model with a different context window or price. Not allowed with auto_compaction false.

state_context.description: Send the newest state-context block stored for the session to this agent's child, in every request. A child collects none of its own. Nothing is sent when the session's statecontext is off or has no block yet.

sandbox.description: The agent's own sandbox: a template name, a template with overrides ({"template": ..., ...}) or an object, written like the setting key sandbox. It is narrowed by the session's: an agent whose sandbox would read, write or reach more than the session's is refused at load, naming the agent, the template and the path; hidden paths and covered tools add up. Without it the agent runs in its caller's sandbox. At run time it is narrowed again by the calling run's, so an agent started by a narrower agent cannot widen it. sandbox.isolation.mode is the isolation key (set only one). An agent whose sandbox is enforcing (bwrap or seatbelt), writes nothing outside {tmp} and that has no profile_message is a reader: it is scheduled, handed off and checkpointed like one.

isolation.description: none (default) runs the child in the session's working directory. worktree runs each run in a git worktree of its own on a detached HEAD, with the files of HEAD (or, with sandbox.isolation.base working, of a snapshot of the session's uncommitted and untracked files), checked out or mounted as an overlay as sandbox.isolation.materialize says. The run's new git objects go to a private folder; in a sandbox the repository's refs, objects and other runs' state are read-only, so it can commit but not make branches or tags. When the run ends, whatever it left is committed (inside the run's sandbox, when it has one), its objects are imported into the repository and the branch worktree.branch_prefix + run id is created; the worktree folder is removed, and a run that changed nothing leaves no branch. The result names the branch with its diff stat and the paths a merge into the session's current HEAD would conflict on. A worktree run changes no file of the session, so it needs no checkpoint and may run beside other runs as an async handle, unless it has MCP tools: their servers act on the session's own folder, so such a run is scheduled as a writer. The path rules apply to the same paths inside the worktree. A resume starts from the branch of the run it continues. Needs a tool that changes files and a working directory inside a git repository with a commit. A child has no read-only mode: its protection is its tool set, its sandbox and this key. A worktree is not a sandbox: without one the child's commands can still reach any absolute path, the session's own folder included.

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock limit of one run, including provider waits.

result_max_bytes.description: Bytes of the child's answer returned per call. A longer answer is cut and the result says so.

list_max_bytes.description: Most bytes of agent list the tool description may carry, which are sent on every request. The full list (name: description) when it fits; else the names alone; else only a count. In the last two the model is told to call subagent without a task to get the list with descriptions, and that call always works. 0 never lists inline. With many agents keep descriptions to one line, or point each session's agents_dir at the folders it needs.

max_concurrent.description: Most children running at once. Children outlive a call, so this counts every child of the same storage_dir across runs; the session that first uses the directory sets it.

keep_finished.description: Finished runs of this session kept readable by id; the oldest are dropped first. Runs still going are never dropped. Counted per session: sessions sharing a storage_dir never drop each other's runs (at startup each session keeps at most the value of the session that opens the storage first).

persist_runs.description: Write a small manifest per run into a .runs folder of storage_dir, so run ids and finished results survive a server restart. A run that was going at the restart is reported as lost; its child died with the server, and only the transcript it wrote remains. false keeps runs in memory only.

deny_agents.description: Names of agents (inline or from agents_dir) removed from the subagent tool: not listed and not launchable. A name that matches no agent is ignored.

delete_transcripts.description: Delete a child's transcript folder from storage_dir when keep_finished drops its run (also at startup), so the folders stop growing. Only a folder directly under storage_dir is deleted. false keeps every transcript. A deleted transcript can no longer give the answer or partial work of its run, but the run was already dropped by then.

background_writers.description: Let an agent that can change files (it lists write, edit, bash, exec or process) run as an async handle: the call honours block_ms and returns a run id, and the run is collected with the async tool like any other. An agent that can change files is handed off only when background_writers is on. Other writers keep running to their end. A handed-off writer keeps changing files after the starting turn ends, so those changes are not in that turn's checkpoint, and a checkpoint restore is refused (409) while one runs. false keeps every writer running to its end.

max_background_writers.description: Most writer runs one session may have going as handles at once (queued ones count). A writer started beyond it is not handed off: the call runs to its end and its result carries a note saying why. Only used with background_writers.

remotes.description: Go backend only. Names of remote entries (files in the remotes folder, see remote.schema.json) whose sub-agents the model may start with agent: "remote:<name>/<session>/<category>/<profile>/<agent>" (session may be left out when the entry has a default_session). The remote runs the agent as that profile's subagent tool would and returns only the final answer; the call is a handle of the async tool, and async wait/status/stop act on the remote run. Each name must have a valid file, checked when the session loads. Default none. The remote's token table decides what is allowed there. A remote agent that changes files changes them on the remote machine, never here, so this server's checkpoint does not cover it.

remote_timeout_ms.description: Longest a remote sub-agent run may take, counted here: past it the run is stopped on the remote and ends as timed_out. The remote agent's own timeout_ms still applies there.

default_block_ms.description: How long a call without block_ms waits for the agent's answer before it returns a run id to collect with async. Clamped to tools.native.async max_block_ms. Longer than the async default_block_ms the other start tools use, since a model run usually outlasts a shell command. A call that other calls of the same response must wait for (the response runs its calls one at a time, as tool_call_scheduling ordered does when it has a call that may change files) waits the async default_block_ms instead.

model_choice.description: Give subagent a model argument and list the calling profile's models in its description, so a call may run an agent on another model the profile lists (optionally @<effort>). false (default) offers no model argument and no model list: the tool's definition is the one it had before the argument existed, a call that names a model is refused, and an agent runs on its own model or the session's model default.

sandbox_choice.description: Sandbox templates (names of files in the session's catalogs.sandbox folder) a subagent call may pick with its sandbox argument; the tool's description lists them with each template's description. A chosen template only narrows: it is narrowed by the agent's own sandbox (or the session's) and by the calling run's, and a choice that would widen it is refused with sandbox_unavailable (widens:). Its isolation.mode worktree puts the run in a worktree of its own; it cannot take an isolated agent out of its worktree. A resume without sandbox keeps the source run's choice. Absent or null (default): no sandbox argument, and the tool's definition is the one it had before the argument existed. An empty list, a duplicate or a name without a template file is refused at load. The MCP servers a run uses are not confined by the choice.

max_depth.description: How many levels of runs may exist below the session. 1 lets only the session start children (a child then has no subagent tool); 2 lets a child start a child of its own. A profile run started by profile_message counts as one level below the run that sent the message, so its sub-agents are counted from there (a remote hop starts again at 0). A start from too deep is refused with subagent_depth_exceeded. profile_message is checked on it too, local or remote, before anything is sent or queued: a message whose run would be deeper than max_depth is refused with profile_depth_exceeded (after a cycle or max_chain refusal). A profile without this section has the default 2; a profile that only sends messages raises it by adding the section with "agents": {} (which also needs tools.native.async) and may deny the subagent tool in its tools block. Not visible to the model.

max_runs_per_root.description: Most runs below one top-level run that may be going at once (queued or running) when children start children, counted across both kinds of run: a profile_message run started from inside the tree (queued or running) and the sub-agents of its target are below the same top-level run. The top-level run keeps its own value as the tree's ceiling: a caller below may narrow it, never widen it. A start beyond it is refused with subagent_limit_reached, a message with profile_limit_reached. Not visible to the model.

max_runs_per_session.description: Most runs one session executes, at any depth, that a start from inside a run may find going: the caller's sub-agents, and the profile_message runs (queued or running) that target the session, counted across every storage folder. The value of the session the new run executes in is checked: the caller's own for its sub-agents, the target's own for a profile_message run (its default 32 when the target has no subagent section). A start beyond it is refused with subagent_limit_reached, a message with profile_limit_reached. A start from inside a child is never queued: with no free slot it is refused with subagent_busy. Not visible to the model.

changed_files_max.description: Most files a sub-agent run lists as changed by its write and edit in the result (written_files); more are only counted (written_files_omitted). 0 turns the list off. Changes made by bash or exec are not listed.

max_queued.description: Runs that may wait for a free slot while max_concurrent are going. A start beyond it is refused with subagent_busy. 0 allows no waiting.

storage_dir.description: Directory holding one transcript folder per child run. A configured relative path resolves from the session cwd (setting.cwd). When omitted, the default lives under the selected profile's tool_storage root (under the cwd when no profile is selected). An absolute path is used as-is. A store is shared by every profile and session that resolves to the same path: an absolute path, or the same configured relative value (which lands in one path under the cwd).

worktree.description: Git worktrees of the agents with isolation worktree.

dir.description: Folder holding one worktree per running run. A relative path resolves from the session's cwd; ~ is expanded. Absent: a jad-worktrees folder inside the repository's git directory, where the session's own search tools never look.

branch_prefix.description: Start of each run's branch name; the run id follows it.

git.description: The git executable: a name looked up in PATH, or a path.

author_name.description: Author name of the commit of a run's changes, used only when the repository has no user.name.

author_email.description: Author email of that commit, used only when the repository has no user.email.

commit_hooks.description: Run the repository's commit hooks for that commit; off commits with --no-verify, so a hook cannot keep a run's work out of its branch.

timeout_ms.description: Limit of each git command, and of the start and the stop of an overlay run's holder (sandbox.isolation.materialize).

collect_attempts.description: How many times jad tries to collect a run's work (commit it and import it into the repository) before it keeps the run's folders for manual recovery and stops retrying: the first try when the run ends, then one at each server start and before each later isolated run. A run whose collection failed is never removed; nothing is deleted after the last attempt either.

statecontext.description: Which of the session's sub-agent runs a statecontext snapshot lists (when statecontext.tools includes subagent), so the model still has its run ids after a compaction (the async provider lists the pending handles of every kind). Each item carries the id, agent, state, a short task preview, times, rounds and tokens; never the answer.

mode.description: items lists the matching records. summary adds a count per state and lists in full only the runs named in detail_states, so a large section stays small; the model fetches the rest with the tool. Counts and the listed records come from one read.

detail_states.description: Only with mode summary: states listed in full, each of which must be in states.

profile_message.description: Go backend only. Lets the model send a message to another profile of the same session and get its final answer, waiting up to block_ms and then continuing as a handle of the async tool (a busy target queues the message, first come first served); that profile keeps its own conversation between calls. The targets are every profile of the caller's session except the caller's own and those in deny_profiles. Needs the tool definition sample/tools/native/profile_message.json. A sub-agent's toolset must not set tools.native.profile_message.

deny_profiles.description: Profile ids (category/name) of the session the model may not message. Ids that are not in the session are ignored. When no other profile remains, the tool cannot be built, so a run or the tools listing of that profile fails with 422; jad check reports it.

timeout_ms.description: Time limit of one call, including the time it is queued behind a busy target.

busy_wait_ms.description: The longest a call may stay queued behind a target that is running before it fails with profile_busy. 0 sets no limit of its own: timeout_ms then bounds the wait. Must not exceed timeout_ms.

default_block_ms.description: How long a call without block_ms waits for the profile's answer before it returns an id to collect with async. Clamped to tools.native.async max_block_ms. A call that other calls of the same response must wait for (the response runs its calls one at a time, as tool_call_scheduling ordered does when it has a call that may change files) waits the async default_block_ms instead.

model_choice.description: Give profile_message a model argument: the model ID (optionally @<effort>) the target profile answers with, one of the models that profile lists. false (default) offers no model argument, so the tool's definition is the one it had before the argument existed and a call that names a model is refused.

sandbox_choice.description: Sandbox templates (names of files in the caller's catalogs.sandbox folder) a profile_message call may pick with its sandbox argument, for the target's run of that message. The template narrows the target's sandbox (already narrowed by the caller's); a choice that would widen it is refused with sandbox_unavailable (widens:). The target's other runs are unaffected. A remote profile refuses it. Absent or null (default): no sandbox argument, and the tool's definition is the one it had before the argument existed. An empty list, a duplicate or a name without a template file is refused at load.

max_queued_per_profile.description: Most calls that may wait for one target profile at once. A call to a busy target joins the queue (first come, first served) and is a queued async handle until the target is free; a call over this number fails at once with profile_busy. 0 queues nobody: a busy target fails at once.

result_max_bytes.description: Most bytes of the target's answer one call returns.

max_chain.description: Longest chain of profiles one message may travel through, the first caller included. 2 lets a profile (or a sub-agent that lists profile_message) message another profile, and that profile's run message no further. A message to a profile already in the chain is refused as a cycle. A cap of its own beside tools.native.subagent.max_depth (default 2 when that section is absent): every message must pass both, so a longer max_chain never lets a chain run deeper than max_depth. Config only: the model never sees it.

sessions.description: Go backend only. Globs (* and ? only, matched against the whole session id, no root prefix) of the other sessions whose profiles the model may message as profile: "<session>/<category>/<profile>". Only sessions that already exist are reached, and a session or profile the globs do not allow answers exactly like one that does not exist. deny_profiles applies in every session. Absent or empty: only the calling session's profiles, as "<category>/<profile>". Config only: the model never sees the globs, only the list of them in the tool description.

remotes.description: Go backend only. Names of remote entries (files in the remotes folder, see remote.schema.json) this profile may message with profile: "remote:<name>/<session>/<category>/<profile>" (session may be left out when the entry has a default_session). Each name must have a valid file, checked when the session loads. Default none: a session reaches no other JAD server unless it lists it. The remote's own token table decides what is allowed there; the call is a handle of the async tool like a local message, and a remote that stays unreachable for the entry's lost_after_ms ends it as lost (the remote run may still be going). A remote answer carries no file paths in the tool's information.

context_trigger.description: Config only. What happens to the target profile's transcript (its messages.jsonl) before a profile_message call. compact is evaluated on EVERY call that starts a run of the target (a queued message when it starts, a sub-agent's call too): it keeps no per-run state, so a target that was empty, below after, or whose compaction failed at one call is looked at again at the next, and one that grows past after again is compacted again. Note that with the default compaction (keep 1 turn, no summary) a compact before every call leaves the target only its previous exchange plus the new message; raise after or the target's compaction keep_turns for a target that should remember more. reset is evaluated the same way, on EVERY call that starts a run of the target (a queued message when it starts, a sub-agent's call too), with no per-run state: it is destructive at every qualifying call, so each message resets the target and drops what the calls before it, including earlier calls of the same run, wrote and answered. A target that was empty at one call (nothing to reset) is reset at the next call once it has content, and a positive after is rechecked at every call. Nothing depends on the calling run: a call with no calling run, or from a run that has ended, is evaluated like any other. Use reset only for a target that should answer every call from a clean history. action: off (default) does nothing; compact compacts the transcript with the target's own compaction settings; reset DELETES the target's whole history and the data derived from it (messages.jsonl, the compaction cache and its backup, the transcript backup, the usage, cursor, run-error and state-context caches and the deleted-history archive) and stops the target's running async handles and sub-agents and drops their unread completion signals, exactly as resetting the profile by hand does. reset is destructive, cannot be undone, and is never on unless you set it here. after: input tokens, default 0. With 0 the target is compacted or reset whenever its messages.jsonl has content, with no token count; with a positive value the action runs only when the last completed response in messages.jsonl itself (never usage-cache.json) had strictly more input tokens, and a transcript with no completed response is left alone. after is accepted, and does nothing, while action is off. A target whose messages.jsonl is missing, empty or blank is left alone (both actions log the warning 'messages.jsonl is empty - nothing to compact' or '... nothing to reset', and the message is still sent; note a compaction leaves the transcript empty until the target answers again, so a reset does NOT clear the compacted history kept in the compaction cache until then). A failed compaction is logged and the message is sent anyway (the next call tries again). A reset that is due and fails (or cannot read the transcript or count tokens) fails closed: the message is NOT sent, the tool call returns context_trigger_failed, the reset is tried again by the next call, and the reset may need attention: it removes the caches, the transcript backup and the archive first and empties messages.jsonl last, so a failure usually leaves the history in place (those files may already be gone) and the next call tries the reset again; if the history was emptied but the directory sync failed, the target's running handles and sub-agents are stopped as for a clean reset, the message is still not sent, and a retry finds the empty transcript and does nothing. Another JAD server's profile (remote:<name>/...) is never compacted or reset: a remote server's profiles are not changed on a caller's behalf, so this setting does not apply to remote targets: with reset the call is refused (context_trigger_unsupported, nothing is sent), with compact the message is sent and the result says the compact was not applied. The legacy compact and compact_after keys were removed and are refused as a config error that names them (compact on is action compact, compact_after is after).

action.description: off, compact or reset, as the description of context_trigger says. reset deletes the target's history.

after.description: Input tokens the target's last completed response in messages.jsonl must have exceeded (strictly more) for the action to run. 0 (default) acts on any target with a non-empty messages.jsonl without counting tokens.

async.description: Go backend only. Enables the async tool (wait, list, status, stop) and the block_ms start argument of process, subagent, tool_smith and exec. process, subagent and tool_smith need this entry: a config that enables any of them without async is rejected; exec does not need it, and without it exec runs to its end. The entry sets the bounds of the async manager that owns the handles of the async tools (process, subagent, tool_smith, exec and profile_message): the live-handle caps, the block and wait times, the size of one response, and how long finished handles and undelivered signals are kept. The tool definition native/async.json must be in tool_definition_paths. Every key has a default, so {} is valid.

max_handles.description: Most live (queued or running) async handles one session may hold. A start at the cap is refused with async_capacity_reached.

max_handles_total.description: Most live async handles on the whole server.

default_block_ms.description: How long a start tool blocks for its result when block_ms is omitted, before it returns a handle. subagent and profile_message have their own default_block_ms.

max_block_ms.description: Largest block_ms a start tool accepts; greater values are clamped. Not below default_block_ms.

default_wait_ms.description: How long the async wait action blocks when wait_ms is omitted. A wait returns as soon as a handle finishes, so a long default costs nothing when work ends early. When it is not set and max_wait_ms is lower, max_wait_ms is the default.

max_wait_ms.description: Largest wait_ms; greater values are clamped. Not below default_wait_ms.

wait_max_signals.description: Most signals one wait returns; the rest stay queued and the response says more.

list_default_limit.description: Page size of the async list action when limit is omitted.

list_max_limit.description: Largest list page; greater limits are clamped. Not below list_default_limit.

summary_max_bytes.description: Most bytes of the summary text in one signal or list entry.

status_summary_max_bytes.description: Most bytes of the summary text the status action returns. Not below summary_max_bytes.

response_max_bytes.description: Byte budget of one async response; entries that do not fit stay queued or on the next page. At least summary_max_bytes + 1024.

keep_finished.description: Terminal handle records kept; the oldest read ones beyond this are deleted with their result files.

retention_days.description: Terminal handle records older than this many days are deleted. 0 turns age pruning off.

unread_max.description: Most undelivered completion signals kept per session; older ones are marked read and counted as dropped. Not below wait_max_signals.

index_flush_ms.description: Delay before the async handle index file is rewritten after a change, so a burst of changes costs one write. The index is only a cache rebuilt from the handle records; 0 writes it at every change.

latest_bytes.description: When a wait returns because block_ms or wait_ms ran out while the work is still going, the most new output per stream (stdout, stderr) a latest block shows, cut at the front with a marker; also the longest line of an agent's activity. Only what is new since the last time that handle's progress was shown. Not above latest_total_bytes.

latest_lines.description: Most activity lines (tool calls and replies) one latest block shows for a sub-agent or profile message that is still going.

latest_total_bytes.description: Most latest-block text one wait, list or status response adds in all, across handles; a handle that does not fit is shown by the next call. Not below latest_bytes.

latest_value_bytes.description: Longest argument value shown in an activity line of a latest block. Not above latest_bytes.

latest_scan_max_bytes.description: Largest transcript a latest block will read to describe an agent's activity; a larger one is not summarized, and the block says so (a sub-agent's block also names the transcript path; a profile_message's result already names it as transcript).

peer_check_ms.description: While this server keeps handles of another running server that shares the same tool storage, how often it checks that the other server still runs; a stopped one's handles then end (with the end it recorded, or as lost) without waiting for an async call, and while it runs its handles' records are read again so an end it recorded (a result, a delete) is taken here. 0 checks only when an async call or a new start reads the handles, and then only whether the other server stopped.

sse_max_ids.description: Most live handle ids the run stream's async_state event carries next to the counts. 0 sends counts only.

stop_wait_ms.description: How long an async stop and a shutdown wait for the work to report that it ended. 0 does not wait. A shutdown waits at least as long as the longest stop of a running exec or tool_smith command (kill_grace_ms + kill_deadline_ms + drain_after_exit_ms).

unread_ttl_days.description: Undelivered signals older than this many days expire. 0 keeps them until the record is pruned.

extension.description: Settings of the extension tools, which call a provider API (decide_systemone and web_search now; fetch API, image API and sound API later). A tool listed here is enabled; a tool not listed is not. Each needs its definition file under extension/ in tool_definition_paths.

web_search.description: Searches the web through a search API and returns result titles, URLs and snippets; fetch reads a result. For models whose provider runs no hosted web_search (Anthropic and Chat Completions models, local models). Read-only. The key is read from api_key_env on each call and never logged. Results are filtered by allowed_domains and blocked_domains; a call may narrow the allowed domains, never widen them, and adds blocked ones. Off unless this key is present. Needs extension.web_search in tool_definition_paths (sample/tools/extension/web_search.json). Do not enable it next to a model.json hosted web_search tool: both use the name web_search.

provider.description: Required. brave: Brave Search API (X-Subscription-Token). tavily: Tavily search API (Bearer key, include/exclude domains sent). searxng: a SearXNG instance's JSON API (format=json must be enabled there); a key, when api_key_env is set, is sent as a Bearer token.

base_url.description: Search endpoint. Defaults: brave https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search, tavily https://api.tavily.com/search. Required for searxng (its /search URL).

api_key_env.description: Environment variable holding the key. Defaults: brave BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY, tavily TAVILY_API_KEY, searxng none.

default_results.description: Results when the call names no max_results; must not be larger than max_results (the default is lowered to max_results when only that is set).

max_results.description: Most results one call returns. Brave returns at most 20 per request.

max_response_bytes.description: A larger search response fails the call.

max_snippet_chars.description: Characters of each snippet shown; 0 shows titles and URLs only.

allowed_domains.description: When not empty, only results on these domains or their subdomains are returned (a leading www. is ignored).

blocked_domains.description: Results on these domains or their subdomains are never returned.

decide_systemone.description: Go backend only. Asks a hosted classifier typed questions (predicate probability, choice, score) about a text and returns the answers; no tools, no free text. Read-only, so a sub-agent can list it in its tools. Off unless this key is present. Needs a key in the environment variable named by api_key_env, read on each call; the model file's key is not used. Needs extension.decide_systemone in tool_definition_paths (sample/tools/extension/decide_systemone.json).

base_url.description: The tool appends path. Default https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha.

path.description: Appended to base_url. /decisions for OpenRouter; /v1/systemone for the TypeSafe API (base_url https://api.typesafe.ai, model jev-latest, api_key_env for example TYPESAFE_API_KEY).

api_key_env.description: Environment variable holding the key. Default OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

max_questions.description: Most questions one call may carry.

max_input_bytes.description: Most bytes one call may send: the input parts plus the questions, as sent.

max_response_bytes.description: Most response bytes read from the provider.

session_files.description: The read-only file list the UI shows for a session's working directory (GET .../files). With enabled false the route answers 403 "file listing is disabled". Objects merge key by key across root defaults, session and profile; ignore_directories replaces the list of the level above.

paths.description: Path rules of the listing and of the transcript, transcripts and profile tools (it was tools.native.read.paths): allow rules add folders outside the working directory, deny rules hide paths. Absent, only the working directory is listed.

enabled.description: Turns the listing on or off.

include_hidden.description: List files and folders whose name starts with a dot.

include_directories.description: List each readable folder too, as its path with a trailing slash (src/). Folders count against max_results.

max_entries.description: Directory entries examined before the listing stops and is marked truncated.

max_results.description: Files returned before the listing stops and is marked truncated.

ignore_directories.description: Folder names that are not entered.

http_debug.description: Optional native HTTP diagnostics written as numbered request/response records under paths.http_debug. With include_request_body or include_response_body, the body is saved raw in a sibling NAME.body file: the request bytes as sent on the wire, the response bytes (the SSE stream) exactly as received, appended as they arrive. The record holds body_file, body_bytes and body_truncated, not the body. max_body_bytes caps each body file. Credential headers (request and response) and credential-like URL query values are written as [REDACTED]. Disabled by default.

max_total_bytes.description: Go backend only. The most the request and response files in the http_debug directory may hold. When a run starts logging, the oldest files beyond it are removed. 0 keeps everything.
